subject: RFP: Tail Latency Measurement & Credit Calculation — Rivermark
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@rivermark.com>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@rivermark.com>, Merritt Legal <legal@rivermark.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: RFP Section 4.2 — Tail-latency & credit calc clarifications

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the RFP response package. A couple of follow-ups from our infra team on SLO measurement:

1) We want to understand how you compute tail-latency for multi-region flows where traffic is routed across US-east and US-west. Do you provide region-weighted percentiles or a global aggregation?

2) On service credits: please confirm whether you apply credits based on absolute breached minutes, or a normalized crediting formula that accounts for probe coverage and traffic weighting. We saw differing approaches in your template.

3) Can you share the cadence and placement of synthetic probes and whether they are used as primary evidence for credit triggers? We need specifics for our audit team (number of probes per region, sampling schedule).

We’d like to resolve these items before the procurement committee next week. Could you provide a written clarification plus any measurement runbooks or probe specs?

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Head of Infrastructure — Rivermark Financial
From: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@rivermark.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@rivermark.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-10T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP Section 4.2 — Tail-latency & credit calc clarifications

Alex —

Appreciate the clear questions. Below is a concise summary; attaching a short measurement proposal and the probe spec workbook for your audit team. If useful we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough.

Summary answers:

- Aggregation model: Redwood exposes both per-region percentiles and a configurable global aggregation. By default our SLO reporting uses region-aware percentiles: we compute p50/p95/p99 within each region and then produce a traffic-weighted global percentile for cross-region SLOs. That traffic-weighting is based on our routing logs during the measurement window.

- Crediting model: We use a normalized credit formula that factors both observed breaches and probe coverage. Credits are proportional to the percentage of affected requests after normalizing for probe-to-production coverage. In practice this prevents over-crediting when probes detect localized routing/peering issues that impact a small fraction of customer traffic. The RFP appendix we sent shows the exact formula; summarized here:
  * credit_minutes = breach_minutes * (estimated_impacted_traffic_fraction / probe_coverage_fraction)
  * cap: credits never exceed the monthly maximum in the contract

- Synthetic probes: Probes are used as supplemental evidence. Primary measurement for credits is production telemetry (sampling of real requests + our inferred regional routing). Where production telemetry is insufficient (e.g., low per-customer volume or opaque routing), synthetic probes are used to corroborate and bound the impacted region. Probe placement: we run a 5x5 mesh (5 vantage points per region, 5 probes per vantage point) every 5 minutes in each production region by default; this is configurable in the dedicated/private deployments.

Attachments: slo-measurement-proposal.pdf, synthetic-probe-specs.xlsx

Next steps: If Rivermark requires probe-only crediting (i.e., synthetic probes as sole evidence), we can propose a narrow amendment but it will alter the crediting factor (higher conservatism) and requires legal approval.

Happy to jump on a call — proposed times: Tue/Wed 10–12 PT.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Reliability & Product Ops
Redwood Inference
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-11T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Draft reply with options for Rivermark — please review

Team —

Drafting our formal response to Alex. Two negotiation options below; choose which to present. I’ll finalize language for procurement/legal once you sign off.

Option A (standard): present region-weighted percentiles + normalized-credit formula (as Evelyn outlined). Probes are supplemental evidence. This keeps current contract language and minimizes financial exposure.

Option B (customer-first): accept probe-primary for credit triggers for the first 3 months of the contract for a 10% premium on committed spend (to offset increased operational risk). Require Rivermark to onboard our probe configurations into their network for cross-checking.

Key technical notes to include in the reply:
- How we compute traffic weights (sampled routing logs over rolling 1-week window)
- Definition of breach minute (minute with >X% of trace samples exceeding latency threshold; X is configurable)
- Probe-to-production calibration procedure (we provide a 7-day calibration window in which we compare probe hits to production traces)

Please comment inline by EOD so we can send a response to Alex tomorrow morning.

- Lauren
Senior Manager, Enterprise Sales Ops
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@rivermark.com>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@rivermark.com>, Merritt Legal <legal@rivermark.com>
Date: 2027-04-13T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP Section 4.2 — Tail-latency & credit calc clarifications

Evelyn / Lauren —

Thanks for the quick follow-up. Rivermark prefers Option B for the proof period. Two clarifications before we can sign off:

1) We need the probe mesh to include two vantage points inside our primary cloud provider (us-east-1) to rule out cross-cloud edge effects. Can Redwood place probes within those provider regions? If not, we’ll ask our network team to allow traffic to/from your public vantage points.

2) Please provide the formal calibration acceptance criteria so our audit team can approve the 7-day calibration window. Specifically: acceptable deviation between probe-derived p99 and production-derived p99 (we propose <10% relative difference).

We’re prepared to accept the 10% premium for the trial, pending legal review of the amendment. Please attach the amendment draft and a sample Excel showing credit calc examples for a 30-day month.

Regards,
Alex
From: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@rivermark.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, Merritt Legal <legal@rivermark.com>
Date: 2027-04-15T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP Section 4.2 — Tail-latency & credit calc clarifications

Alex —

Appreciate the direction. Action items and deliverables attached. Quick summary:

- Probe placement: Redwood can provision two private probes in us-east-1 via our cloud-partner program for the trial. We’ll need an IP allowlist from your team and a short coordination call to complete setup.

- Calibration acceptance: we propose the following metrics for the 7-day calibration window:
  * median relative difference (probe vs production) on p95 <= 6%
  * median relative difference on p99 <= 12%
  * no more than 8 hours cumulative window where relative difference > 25% (to catch transient routing flaps)
  These thresholds are conservative and intended to give both sides confidence.

- Attached: amendment_draft_RIV_probe_trial.docx and an example credit-calculation workbook (synthetic-probe-specs.xlsx includes worked examples). Also attached is a small CSV with our initial probe run results from a mirror test environment (rmpoc-probe-results-20270414.csv).

If that looks good, we’ll have Legal prepare the final amendment and our infra team will open a ticket for probe provisioning. Proposed next call: Fri 04/16 9:00 PT to confirm IPs and timelines.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Reliability & Product Ops
Redwood Inference
